{{c|''As he promi{{ls}}ed, he giueth them a {{ls}}ight of the glorie, vnto which Suffering doth bring: 9 and then againe doth inculcate his Pa{{ls}}sion. 14 A deuil al{{ls}}o he ca{{ls}}teth out which his Di{{ls}}ciples could not for their incredulitie and lacke of praying and fa{{ls}}ting. 22 being yet in Galilee, he reuealeth more about his Pa{{ls}}sion. 24 and the tribute that the Collectors exacted for al, he payeth for him {{ls}}elf and Peter: declaring yet withal his freedom both by word and miracle.''}}

{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The {{sc|Transfigvration}} of our Lord, celebrated in the Church the 6. of Aug. The Go{{ls}}pel of the {{ls}}aid fea{{ls}}t, & of the 2. Sunday in Lent: and on the Saterday before.}}{{dropinitial|A|fl={{verse|chapter=17|verse=1}}}}{{sc|Nd}} after {{ls}}ix dayes {{sc|Iesvs}} taketh vnto him Peter and Iames and Iohn his brother, and bringeth them into a high mountaine apart:{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 9, 2. Luc. 9, 28.''}} {{verse|chapter=17|verse=2}} And he vvas {{sup|‖}} transfigured before them. And his face did {{ls}}hine as the {{ls}}unne: & his garments became vvhite as {{ls}}now.{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''2. Pet. 1, 17.''}} {{verse|chapter=17|verse=3}} And behold there {{sup|‖}} appeared to them Moy{{ls}}es and Elias talking vvith him. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=4}} And Peter an{{ls}}vvering, {{ls}}aid to {{sc|Iesvs}}, Lord, it is good for vs to be here: if thou vvilt, let vs make here three tabernacles, one for thee, and one for Moy{{ls}}es, and one for Elias. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=5}} And as he vvas yet {{ls}}peaking, behold a bright cloude ouer{{ls}}hadovved them. And loe a voice out of the cloude, {{ls}}aying. This is my vvelbeloued {{ls}}onne, in vvhom I am vvel plea{{ls}}ed: heare ye him. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=6}} And the di{{ls}}ciples hearing it, fel vpon their face, and vvere {{ls}}ore afraid. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=7}} And {{sc|Iesvs}} came and touched them: and he {{ls}}aid to them, Ari{{ls}}e, and feare not. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=8}} And they lifting vp their eyes, {{ls}}avv no body, but only {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=9}} And as they de{{ls}}cended from the {{sup|‖}} mount, {{sc|Iesvs}} commaunded them, {{ls}}aying, Tel the vi{{ls}}ion to no body, til the Sonne of man be ri{{ls}}en from the dead.⊣

{{verse|chapter=17|verse=10}} And his Di{{ls}}ciples a{{ls}}ked him, {{ls}}aying, What {{ls}}ay the Scribes then, that {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mal. 4, 5.''}}* Elias mu{{ls}}t come fir{{ls}}t? {{verse|chapter=17|verse=11}} But he an{{ls}}vvering, {{ls}}aid to them, {{sup|‖}} Elias in deede {{ls}}hal come, and re{{ls}}tore al things. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=12}} And I {{ls}}ay to you, that Elias is already come, and they did not knovv him, but vvrought on him vvhat{{ls}}oeuer they vvould. So al{{ls}}o the Sonne of man {{ls}}hal {{ls}}uffer of them. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=13}} Then the Di{{ls}}ciples vnder{{ls}}toode, that of Iohn the Bapti{{ls}}t he had {{ls}}poken to them.

{{verse|chapter=17|verse=14}} And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mar. 9, 14. Luc. 9, 37.''}}* vvhen he vvas come vnto the multitude, there came to him a man falling dovvne vpon his knees before him, {{verse|chapter=17|verse=15}} {{ls}}aying, Lord haue mercie vpon my {{ls}}onne, for he is lunatike, and {{ls}}ore vexed: for he falleth often into the fire, and often into the vvater. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=16}} and I offered him to thy Di{{ls}}ciples: and they could not cure him. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=17}} {{sc|Iesvs}} an{{ls}}vvered and {{ls}}aid, O faithles and peruer{{ls}}e generation, hovv long {{ls}}hal I be vvith<noinclude>{{continues|you?}}</noinclude>
